data.content_ref: inline:The proposed dependence rests on an unsupported factual premise: SRC_001 asserts that 0094852dcac7 'reuses the same observable vocabulary (packages, failing tests, caught mutations)' from SRC_003's metrics schema, but provided no quoted evidence from either artifact showing this shared vocabulary actually appears in 0094852dcac7. If 0094852dcac7 does not in fact reference packages/failing tests/caught mutations, the entire dependence claim collapses. Moreover, the refutation condition is self-servingly weak: it is only refuted if 0094852dcac7 'invents a wholly disjoint measurement language' — a condition that would essentially never hold for any artifact in the same broad domain, since sharing even one generic term like 'tests' would salvage the claim. This makes the relation unfalsifiable in practice: any two testing-related artifacts share some vocabulary, so the refutation clause cannot genuinely discriminate. The problem demands a relation 'stating what it is REFUTED IF' meaningfully; a refutation condition satisfiable only by an artifact with zero lexical overlap provides no real discriminating power.
